title: test(runtime): pin the /data door's 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT for a sharing_rule row created or renamed under a declared rule's name
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuACdPWFJTLDcTrByFCHLzqb)_

Fixes #25253

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What

Adds one end-to-end suite, `packages/runtime/src/sharing-rule-declared-name.data-door.pin.test.ts`. It boots the composition `bootStack` mirrors (ObjectQL, sqlite-wasm in memory, Hono, the app, platform objects, auth, security, sharing, REST, dispatcher). The application declares two sharing rules through its own `sharingRules`. A signed-in administrator then drives the generic `/data` door over HTTP:

- `POST /api/v1/data/sys_sharing_rule` under a declared rule's name answers `409` with `code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, and no row lands.
- `PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_sharing_rule/:id` renaming an authored row onto a declared rule's name answers `409` with `code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, and the row keeps its name.
- **Control:** the same `POST` under a name no declaration holds answers 2xx and the row lands. So the 409 comes from the guard and not from the rig.
- **Precondition:** the sharing-rule service the guard asks (`declaredRuleNamed`) reads both declared rules, and neither has a row.

This is test-only. No production file changed and there is no behaviour change. Today the door does answer 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` on both paths, so `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` (regime C) is accurate.

**Wire shape, measured rather than assumed.** The `/data` door answers its flat envelope: `{ error: "SENTENCE", code: "RESOURCE_CONFLICT", object: "sys_sharing_rule" }`. `code` sits at the top level (`mapDataError`, `@objectstack/types`), and the pin reads it there. It does not use a fallback that would also accept a nested `error.code`. The first run asserted the nested spelling and went red on exactly that.

**Why each refusal has its own declared rule.** `sys_sharing_rule`'s unique constraint on the name also answers `409`, as `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`. My first draft used one declared name for both cases. Under ablation the create landed, and the rename then answered `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, so a status-only pin would have read that 409 as the guard's. Now each case targets its own declared rule and stays independent under ablation. `code` is asserted beside `status`.

## Lane: runtime, not plugin-sharing (deviation from the claim's file surface)

The claim's file surface was `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/**` test files, based on the assumption that `business-unit-parent-delete-restrict.test.ts` is an HTTP rig. I measured it, and it is not. It drives `engine.delete` on a real ObjectQL + SqlDriver, and `/api/v1/data/...` appears only in a comment. plugin-sharing has no `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` or `@objectstack/runtime` dependency. `@objectstack/runtime` depends on plugin-sharing, so adding runtime as a dev dependency would create a workspace cycle. An HTTP pin in plugin-sharing would therefore need new dependencies and a hand-built door. The card names "plugin-sharing or runtime" as the lane, and runtime already carries every piece: its full-composition pins (`unresolved-object-name.actions-door.pin.test.ts`, `hook-handler-package-scope.pin.test.ts`) use the same boot. So the suite lives there. It adds no new testkit or helper file.

## Evidence (head a949814796)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/sharing-rule-declared-name.data-door.pin.test.ts` gave Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 4 passed (4).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` gave Test Files 436 passed (436), Tests 6889 passed | 19 skipped. The lock reported VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` exited 0. The pin is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`--listFilesOnly` count 1) and carries no ledger entry, so it compiles with zero errors.
- **Ablation, one round, guard disabled.** The runtime suite resolves `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` through `dist/`, so each leg rebuilt it.
  - `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the `bindDeclaredRuleNameGuard` throw (`if (declared) throw new DeclaredSharingRuleNameConflictError(...)`) with a marker assignment. On disk: anchor x1 to x0, blob 26f18e1e7c30 to d5199123b3f6.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing build` ran, then `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/plugin-sharing __ABLATION_25253` reported the marker present in 2 built files.
  - The pin then went **2 failed | 2 passed**. The create case read `expected 201 to be 409` and the rename case read `expected 200 to be 409`. The precondition and the control stayed green, as predicted.
  - Restore: blob back to the HEAD blob 26f18e1e7c30, and `git diff HEAD` was empty. I rebuilt, and `--absent` reported the marker absent from all 6 built files, with the tree clean against HEAD. The pin went back to 4 passed (4).

## Changeset

None. This PR carries `skip-changeset` because it publishes nothing. `packages/runtime`'s `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. After a runtime build, the pin's own fixture name `pin_amber_projects_declared` has 0 hits there, and the positive control `createDispatcherPlugin` has 4 hits in `dist/`.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 53 families for this diff. I ran each one under the verify lock and recorded its exit code. `--ran` reports: 53 accounted for, 52 run (all exit 0), 1 NOT MEASURED. The NOT MEASURED one is `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) because it reads every package's `dist/` and this checkout built only runtime's closure. This diff changes no built output. CI runs it.

## Acceptance notes

- **File wall.** One run of this file reads `Duration 15.6–16.8 s`, of which `import` is about 14 s and `tests` about 2 s. That is over the 10 s file line, and the cost is the full-composition boot, the same one the sibling runtime pins pay. I declared no budget line: none of the three ruled classes fits. This note is for the shard-timings refresh, which reports and never reds.
- **Envelope dialects.** The sharing-rule route (`POST /sharing/rules`) answers this refusal in the nested envelope (`error.code`), while the `/data` door answers it flat (`code`). This is not a defect for this card. It is the known two-dialect split, recorded here so nobody asserts the wrong spelling on the wrong door.
